answer: Treat the network as a lagoon where nothing is heard until it echoes. A newcomer may claim a job, but it only counts when three strangers who saw the same event echo it back, each signing the same hash, and every echo stays in the lagoon's public record. To speak at all, each identity must crack open a walnut: a small, hard-shelled deposit returned after a dozen corroborated echoes, and shattered — burned — if any echo is proved false. A farmer minting a thousand faces needs a thousand real jobs, three thousand witnesses, and a thousand walnuts that crack together when one lie is caught.
